claims.statement: Hexarelin is a synthetic hexapeptide GHRP-class growth hormone secretagogue that stimulates growth hormone release both in vitro and in vivo by acting as a ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a) agonist.

extractedEvidence.quote: Hexarelin is a new hexapeptide (His-D-2-methyl-Trp-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2) that stimulates the release of growth hormone both in vitro and in vivo.

Hexarelin is a synthetic hexapeptide that is primarily of interest in the field of endocrinology research. It functions as a ghrelin receptor agonist, which makes it a useful tool for studying the regulation of growth hormone release and appetite control mechanisms.

claims.statement: In a double-blind, placebo-controlled, rising-dose study of 12 healthy adult male volunteers, single intravenous boluses of hexarelin (0.5, 1, and 2 micrograms/kg) produced dose-dependent increases in plasma growth hormone, peaking at about 30 minutes; mean peak GH concentrations were 3.9 (placebo), 26.9, 52.3, and 55.0 ng/mL at increasing doses, with response near-maximal by the 2 microgram/kg dose. This is an acute GH-release pharmacodynamic finding in healthy men, not evidence of any downstream clinical benefit.

context.doseText: single IV bolus of 0.5, 1, or 2 micrograms/kg in a rising-dose study design (trial protocol; not a use recommendation)

extractedEvidence.quote: Twelve adult male volunteers received single intravenous boluses of 0.5, 1 and 2.micrograms.kg-1 hexarelin as well as placebo.
The mean peak plasma growth hormone concentrations (Cmax) were 3.9, 26.9, 52.3, 55.0 ng.ml-1 after 0, 0.5, 1 and 2 micrograms.kg-1, respectively.

reviewFlags: acute GH pharmacodynamic endpoint only; no downstream clinical outcome (body composition, strength, disease outcome) was measured in this trial
small single-dose acute study (n=12); not generalizable to chronic subcutaneous self-administration protocols marketed online

claimType efficacy is not on the directive's fieldAuthorityRequired list (regulatory, safety-critical, monitoring, product-specific dosing, formulation, storage/reconstitution); no FDA/DailyMed document exists for this trial since hexarelin has no FDA-approved product, so fieldAuthorityRequired remains false

independent review (systematic review, Sexual Medicine Reviews PMID 28400207) corroborates the class's dose-dependent acute GH pharmacology and reinforces that few long-term controlled studies exist for GHSs; the exact numeric Cmax figures (3.9/26.9/52.3/55.0 ng/mL) could not be independently re-verified outside the original Imbimbo 1994 controlled-human-study source

claims.statement: In a rat model of myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury (left coronary artery ligation), subcutaneous hexarelin (100 mcg/kg/day for 7 days) improved cardiac systolic function, reduced malondialdehyde production, and increased surviving cardiomyocytes versus control, an effect blocked by a GHSR antagonist and attributed to interleukin-1 pathway modulation. This is preclinical rodent data and does not establish a cardioprotective effect in humans.

claims.statement: In a dose-response study of intravenous hexarelin (0-1.0 micrograms/kg) in healthy adult men (Massoud et al. 1996, J Clin Endocrinol Metab), hexarelin produced dose-dependent increases in prolactin (up to 180% above baseline, ED50 0.39 micrograms/kg) and a step increase in cortisol of approximately 40% at doses of 0.5 micrograms/kg and above, in addition to growth hormone release. In a separate 16-week chronic twice-daily subcutaneous dosing study (Rahim et al. 1999, Clinical Endocrinology), the cortisol response to hexarelin decreased over the treatment course and prolactin levels remained stable, with the authors concluding that clinically significant over-stimulation of the pituitary-adrenal axis and prolactin secretion did not occur at the doses used. Taken together, hexarelin has demonstrated measurable acute effects on cortisol and prolactin beyond the GH axis, though the only located chronic-dosing study did not find clinically significant HPA-axis over-stimulation at the studied dose.
